originalTitle: Netanyahu rejects Trump’s Gaza plan and vows no withdrawal until Hamas disarms – as it happened
summary: This live blog is now closed.
content: We’re wrapping our live coverage of the Middle East crisis for today. Here are Sunday’s top developments: Israel has rebuffed Donald Trump’s Gaza plan. The country said it would not leave Gaza unless Hamas was “genuinely” disarmed. Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said that they were discussing their concerns with the US. “They have ideas; some of them are acceptable to us and some are not, and we know how to stand our ground on these matters,” Netanyahu said. Donald Trump said he’s “low keying it” with Iran as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed. Trump’s comments to Axios came after Iran said it would not agree to a deal until the US met its demands, which included never speaking insulting the country. “We are only semi-negotiating with them,” Trump also told Axios. Although Donald Trump has rebuffed claims that the US is running low on weapons crucial to its war on Iran, a leaked memo indicates that his military leadership is concerned by falling stockpiles. Per the Washington Post, deputy US defense secretary Steve Feinberg on Wednesday told defense industry leaders that they must “drive significantly faster, more aggressive delivery schedules and/or increased production for critical capabilities.” Meanwhile, Trump’s war on Iran continues to draw prominent criticism in the US. New York’s Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez said Trump’s complaints about rising costs clash with his policies that has made daily life more expensive. “Donald Trump may be saying that oil companies are making too much money, but what Donald Trump is doing is starting a reckless war in Iran, having closed door meetings with oil companies before his election, saying, you know, you give me money, you give me campaign contributions, and I will do whatever you want,” Ocasio-Cortez said on ABC. Iran’s supreme leader, Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei, has selected a former commander of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to represent him on the nation’s supreme security council, CNN reported. Mohsen Rezaei, whom CNN described as a “senior Iranian military adviser”, will replace Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr in this position, per CNN. Khamenei described Rezaei as a leader of the “Sacred Defense” which, CNN notes, is Iran’s way of referring to the 1988 Iran-Iraq war. In the official decree about Rezaei’s appointment, Khamenei expressed thanks to Zolghadr for his work. As CNN points out, it’s not known whether Rezaei’s appointment will affect Iran’s demands of the US to reopen the strait of Hormuz. An Israeli tank has invaded the town of Hadatha, southern Lebanon, with troops accused of setting buildings on fire, according to the Lebanese state-owned National News Agency. Iran’s president, Masoud Pezeshkian, recently met with supreme leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, who has not appeared in public since assuming the post early in the Middle East war, Khamenei’s office said on Sunday. “Dr Masoud Pezeshkian met Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei and spoke with him at the start of his third year in the presidency,” the supreme leader’s office said in a statement, without indicating the date of the meeting. Pezeshkian, who took office in July 2024, said in early May that he met with Khamenei, also without specifying the date, but the supreme leader’s office did not issue any statements at the time. The president had said on Wednesday that communication with Khamenei was “very difficult at the moment”, and speculation has swirled about the supreme leader’s health after he was reportedly wounded in strikes that killed his father. Khamenei’s office said the two “discussed in detail the country’s issues and problems”, including the “current military situation and future prospects”. Donald Trump on Sunday suggested that he’s going to let economic pressures prompt Iran to reopen the strait of Hormuz rather than launch another military action. “We are low keying it,” Trump told Axios. Trump’s comments came hours after Iran said that it wouldn’t reopen the crucial waterway unless the US met its demands – which included never insulting or threatening the country, per Axios. “We are only semi-negotiating with them,” Trump also told the news website. “We are just watching Iran with its huge inflation and the fact they have no money.” Trump, who said Iran “is in very bad shape”, claimed that Americans are feeling less financial pressures from the war because oil prices are down. “It will work out. It always works out. It’s like a chess game,” Trump also reportedly said. Donald Trump has rejected claims that the US is running low on munitions in its war with Iran – but a new report indicates that his military leadership is pushing defense companies to ramp up weapons production. According to the Washington Post, the deputy US defense secretary Steve Feinberg on Wednesday told defense industry heads that they must “drive significantly faster, more aggressive delivery schedules and/or increased production for critical capabilities.” Feinberg’s written directive to defense industry leaders said they had to present a plan within 21 days on how to increase production. Feinberg’s instruction was in a memo obtained by the Washington Post. “Years-long development cycles are not acceptable,” Feinberg reportedly wrote. “We must dramatically accelerate our program schedules and expand our production capacity now.” The Pentagon’s chief spokesperson, Sean Parnell, confirmed that this memo is “real” and “will inform the fiscal year 2028 budget submitted to Congress for funding, and it is entirely consistent with our ongoing push to rebuild the defense industrial base”, per the newspaper. Syria and Russia have made a deal about the Kremlin’s military presence in the Middle Eastern nation, according to reports. Russia has had a military presence in Syria since the Soviet era, but its standing there came into question after rebels ousted Bashar al-Assad some two years ago, according to the New York Times. chineseContent: 我们今天即将结束对中东危机的现场报道。以下是周日的主要事态发展：以色列拒绝了唐纳德·特朗普的加沙计划。该国表示，除非哈马斯“真正”解除武装，否则不会离开加沙。以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡表示，他们正在与美国讨论他们的担忧。内塔尼亚胡说：“他们有想法；其中有些我们可以接受，有些则不可以，我们知道如何在这些问题上坚持自己的立场。”唐纳德·特朗普表示，由于霍尔木兹海峡仍然关闭，他对伊朗“低调”。特朗普对 Axios 发表上述言论之前，伊朗表示，在美国满足其要求（包括不得发表侮辱该国的言论）之前，不会同意达成协议。 “我们只是与他们进行半谈判，”特朗普还告诉 Axios。尽管唐纳德·特朗普否认了美国对伊朗战争至关重要的武器不足的说法，但一份泄露的备忘录表明，他的军事领导层对库存下降感到担忧。据《华盛顿邮报》报道，美国国防部副部长史蒂夫·范伯格周三告诉国防工业领导人，他们必须“显着加快、更积极地推进交付计划和/或增加关键能力的生产”。与此同时，特朗普对伊朗的战争继续在美国引起强烈批评。纽约的亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯表示，特朗普对成本上涨的抱怨与他的政策相冲突，这些政策使日常生活变得更加昂贵。 “唐纳德·特朗普可能会说石油公司赚了太多钱，但唐纳德·特朗普正在做的是在伊朗发动一场鲁莽的战争，他在当选前与石油公司举行闭门会议，说，你知道，你给我钱，你给我竞选捐款，我会做任何你想做的事，”奥卡西奥-科尔特斯在美国广播公司表示。伊朗
